**4B.4 Research Note: Bola Ahmed Tinubu (2024)**

Bottom line: **mixed to negative**. I found some **institutional-reform rhetoric and a few concrete corrective actions**, especially around policing oversight and the judiciary. But the year’s stronger pattern is **punitive handling of dissent, pressure on journalists, and reactive rather than durable accountability**. I found **no strong 2024 evidence** that Tinubu meaningfully strengthened legislatures or audit bodies.

- [President Tinubu to Judiciary: Our Justice System Must Guarantee Well-being Of Nigerians, Economic Growth](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-to-judiciary-our-justice-system-must-guarantee-well-being-of-nigerians-economic-growth/) | State House | 2024-04-24  
  Tinubu urged judiciary reform around inclusivity, fairness, rule of law, and anti-corruption. This is positive evidence that he publicly endorsed a stronger court system, but it is rhetorical and does not by itself show that he empowered courts when they constrained him.  
  Question IDs: `4B.4`, also `3B.4`

- [My Resolve To Enhance Nigeria’s Security Unwavering President Tinubu](https://statehouse.gov.ng/my-resolve-to-enhance-nigerias-security-unwavering-president-tinubu/) | State House | 2024-04-22  
  Tinubu backed state policing and framed decentralization as a way to improve accountability and safeguard civil liberties. This is the clearest positive signal for oversight-by-design, because it points toward more local accountability rather than pure central control.  
  Question IDs: `4B.4`, also `3B.4`, `3B.8`

- [President Tinubu appoints new leadership for Police Service Commission and Nigerian Police Trust Fund](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-appoints-new-leadership-for-police-service-commission-and-nigerian-police-trust-fund/) | State House | 2024-06-10  
  Tinubu appointed new leadership for the Police Service Commission and Police Trust Fund. This supports a limited positive reading on oversight institutions because it can strengthen civilian supervision capacity over policing, though the announcement does not describe an enforcement mechanism.  
  Question IDs: `4B.4`, also `3B.4`

- [President Tinubu Orders Probe Of Security Agents Involved In Arrest, Detention Of Minors](https://www.thecable.ng/tinubu-orders-probe-of-security-agents-involved-in-arrest-detention-of-minors/) | TheCable | 2024-11-04  
  Tinubu ordered an investigation into the arrest, detention, and treatment of minors detained over the protests, created an administrative review process, and said involved officers could be disciplined. This is the strongest direct positive evidence for 4B.4, but it is reactive and came after public outrage.  
  Question IDs: `4B.4`, also `3B.4`

- [UNICEF welcomes President Tinubu’s order for immediate release of detained children](https://www.unicef.org/nigeria/press-releases/unicef-welcomes-president-tinubus-order-immediate-release-detained-children) | UNICEF Nigeria | 2024-11-05  
  UNICEF confirmed Tinubu ordered the release of detained children and young people. This corroborates a corrective step, but it still looks like damage control rather than durable strengthening of oversight institutions.  
  Question IDs: `4B.4`, also `3B.4`

- [Detained End-bad-governance suspects released as Shettima hands over pardoned suspects to state governments](https://fmino.gov.ng/detained-endbad-governance-suspects-released-vice-president-shettima-hands-over-pardoned-suspects-to-state-governments/) | Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation | 2024-11-05  
  The ministry said the detainees were released under Tinubu’s directive and handed to state governments for rehabilitation and reintegration. This supports a partial corrective response, but it still does not show a standing accountability system that constrained the executive earlier.  
  Question IDs: `4B.4`, also `3B.4`

- [Nigeria charges protesters with treason, inciting military](https://theprint.in/world/nigeria-charges-protesters-with-treason-inciting-military/2249248/) | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-09-02  
  Prosecutors charged protesters with treason and mutiny after the August demonstrations. This is negative evidence because it shows legal institutions being used punitively against dissent, not clearly strengthened as independent checks on power.  
  Question IDs: `4B.4`, also `4B.2`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`

- [Nigeria: Police used excessive force to violently quash #EndBadGovernance protests](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/nigeria-police-used-excessive-force-to-violently-quash-endbadgovernance-protests/) | Amnesty International | 2024-11-28  
  Amnesty documented killings, mass detentions, and torture during the crackdown, and said authorities denied wrongdoing. This is strong negative evidence for 4B.4 because it shows a lack of effective oversight and accountability over security forces.  
  Question IDs: `4B.4`, also `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `3B.10`

- [Nigeria: Protesters Charged with Treason](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/06/nigeria-protesters-charged-treason) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-09-06  
  HRW said protesters, including children, were held for long periods and charged with treason, with due-process concerns. This is negative evidence that the state response remained punitive rather than institutionally restrained.  
  Question IDs: `4B.4`, also `4B.2`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`

- [Nigeria police charge 4 journalists with cybercrimes for corruption reporting](https://cpj.org/2024/10/nigeria-police-charge-4-journalists-with-cybercrimes-for-corruption-reporting/) | Committee to Protect Journalists | 2024-10-03  
  CPJ reported that four journalists were charged under the Cybercrimes Act despite February reform. This is negative evidence for oversight, because it shows legal tools still being used against investigative reporting.  
  Question IDs: `4B.4`, also `4B.3`, `4B.2`, `3B.8`

- [Nigeria: Freedom on the Net 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/nigeria/freedom-net/2024) | Freedom House | 2024  
  Freedom House said the Cybercrimes Act’s cyberstalking provision had frequently been used against journalists and activists, contributing to takedowns and self-censorship. This is negative evidence that oversight institutions were not being insulated from executive pressure.  
  Question IDs: `4B.4`, also `4B.2`, `4B.3`, `3B.8`

**Search gap**
- I found **no strong 2024 evidence** that Tinubu meaningfully strengthened **legislatures** or **audit bodies** in ways that constrained him.
- I also found **no clear evidence** of concrete reforms that made **courts** more independent beyond broad rule-of-law rhetoric and the later probe/release episode.
- The available record is therefore heavier on **policing, protest, and media pressure** than on durable institutional strengthening.
